# README, CONTRIBUTING and docs pages

Badges, the title and a generated table of contents are layout, so leave them alone and work on the content.
Keep a hand-written table of contents in step with the sections.

## Reader path

The repository decides the structure.

- Keep the existing structure as long as a reader can follow it in this order.
- The order is what the project is and whether they need it, how to start, how to use it for their tasks, then the reference.
- Propose a restructure of the part that breaks that path and ask before doing it.
- Ask before renaming a section, since other docs and sites may link to its anchor.

For the content you write, these hold.

- The intro says in one to three sentences what the project is and what the reader gets from it, before anything else in the content.
- Getting started ends on something the reader can see working.
- Getting started uses numbered steps when they must run in order.
- Name a new section after what the reader wants to do or know, such as "Running behind a reverse proxy" or "Rotating credentials".
- Prefer that over a generic name such as "Usage" or "Advanced".
- Document a limitation only when the code or an issue shows it, and add no section for it otherwise.
- Order the columns of a new options table name, required, default, description, and keep the order of an existing one.

## Kinds of content

A README may hold every kind of content, but each section stays one kind.

| Kind        | Serves                | Holds                                        |
| ----------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Tutorial    | a newcomer learning   | one guided path that works end to end        |
| How-to      | someone with a goal   | the steps for that goal and their caveats    |
| Reference   | someone looking it up | complete, dry facts, often a table           |
| Explanation | someone asking why    | the reasoning, the tradeoffs, the background |

A how-to that grows a parameter table, or setup steps that turn into design rationale, is drift.

- Propose moving the foreign part to a section of its kind with a one-sentence link left behind, and ask before doing it.
- Keep the why as one sentence next to the rule instead, only when that sentence is all the foreign part adds.
- When a README grows into several long guides, propose splitting them into the docs site or separate files linked from the README.
- Ask before doing that split.

## Sets of items

A set is a group of parallel items such as skills, commands or options.

- Give each item its own heading when it needs a paragraph, so the reader can scan, link and jump to it.
- Give each item a one-sentence bullet that names it inside the sentence ("The `--verbose` flag prints every request"), when it needs only one sentence.
- Name the heading after the item.
- Cover the same points under every item (what it does, when you reach for it, how you start it), in wording that varies from one item to the next.
- Treat every item of the set the same way, in the form that the longest item needs.

## CONTRIBUTING

It serves contributors, so it holds what a first change needs and nothing a user needs.

- How to set up the project.
- How to run the checks and regenerate files.
- How changes get versioned and released.
- Where each kind of file goes.

## Docs site pages

- Follow the frontmatter and the shortcodes of the sibling pages.
- Translate rather than paraphrase when updating the other languages of a page.
- Build the site after the change when the repository defines a build command.
